source.title: Label Noise SGD Provably Prefers Flat Global Minimizers
source.authors: Alexandru Damian; Tengyu Ma; J. Lee

record.file_problem: The full paper text is supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper's theoretical and experimental results examine optimization and training behavior under label-noise SGD, including on ResNet18/CIFAR-10. The experiments use label noise to escape poor zero-training-loss initializations, a different question and outcome from whether training from random initialization reaches near-zero training error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that the experiments start from two already zero-training-loss initializations. Its statement that overparameterized networks can easily achieve zero training loss in the kernel regime is attributed to prior work and is not a result of this study. Training accuracy in Figure 3 is described, but no separate numeric training-accuracy values are stated in the supplied text; the reported experimental outcome is test accuracy and Hessian trace.
record.test_reason: The main experiments concern implicit regularization, but the study also reports its own ResNet18 training reaching 100% training accuracy on CIFAR-10 and interpolating an augmented CIFAR-10 dataset with random labels. These preparatory training outcomes bear on V1. Starting subsequent experiments at selected global minimizers alone would not establish this.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct for the experiments. The principal theoretical conclusion is convergence to a neighborhood of an approximate stationary point of a regularized loss under smoothness, learning-rate separation, KL, and near-minimizer initialization assumptions. It does not guarantee convergence to a flat global minimizer in every run. The experiments show improved generalization and reduced curvature proxies, with stronger regularization at larger learning rates.
record.recipe_differences: The claim concerns training from random initialization until near-zero training error; this study analyzes label-noise SGD's implicit regularization and experimentally starts from already zero-training-loss solutions. Its CIFAR-10 experiments use randomized label flipping and measure test accuracy and Hessian trace.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper says regularization strength is strongly correlated with learning rate. It varies the maximum learning rate and compares runs with and without momentum; the reported test-accuracy outcome also differs by initialization (reaches the baseline from the full-batch initialization and comes within 1% from the adversarial initialization).

fits_no_version.finding: Label-noise SGD improves test accuracy from two poor-generalizing training minimizers; larger learning rates produce stronger implicit regularization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label-noise SGD can move ResNet18 with GroupNorm on CIFAR-10 from interpolating solutions toward flatter, better-generalizing solutions.

fits_no_version.finding: Momentum experiments improve performance relative to experiments without momentum; the theory predicts increased effective regularization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum strengthens the implicit regularization of label-noise SGD in the tested setup.

record.problems: The experiments use only ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 and begin from two already zero-training-loss initializations, so they do not test the claim's random-initialization training outcome. They report medians over 3 seeds with min/max ranges, but the supplied text gives no exact numerical values for the plotted test accuracy or Hessian trace. GroupNorm replaces BatchNorm to maintain independence of sample gradients.
record.rows_left_out: No separately stated numeric training-accuracy result is given in the text; Figure 3 describes training accuracy but the supplied prose reports test accuracy and Hessian trace. Figure 4's momentum-specific outcomes are figure-only, so their rows record the reported measurements without assigning numeric values.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100; size comparisons; early stopping and regularization comparisons; Adam; training-error trajectories and seed variability for the preparatory runs. Random initialization is explicit for the full-batch run but not separately specified for random-label memorization.
All parts: no two-layer ReLU teacher-student width comparison or spurious-minimum frequencies.
All parts: no depth comparison or shortcut intervention.
All parts: no activation-matched initialization comparison or trainable-depth result. Appendix C concerns kernel-regime convergence rather than signal-preserving initialization.

All parts: no measured recovery above an initial stability threshold, edge-of-stability trajectory, or below-threshold divergence. Appendix A explicitly excludes explaining optimization above the quadratic stability bound.
All parts: GroupNorm replaces BatchNorm without a normalization comparison.

missing.what: The study's own preparatory training outcomes: full-batch training from random initialization achieves 100% training accuracy; SGD also interpolates 500,000 augmented CIFAR-10 images assigned random labels. Record these separately from the selected initial conditions of R1–R4. The random-label recipe uses batch size 256, learning rate 0.01, and 300 epochs.
missing.locator: Section 4, initialization descriptions; Appendix D, preparatory training recipes

record.verdict_notes: Figures 3 and 4 inconsistently call the left panels training accuracy in their captions; their axes and surrounding prose identify test accuracy. Do not treat those curves as training-error evidence. The V1 verdict rests on separately reported preparatory training outcomes, not the main experiment rows or cited NTK results.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test reaching near-zero training classification error from random initialization, corrupted or random labels, CIFAR-100, or the stated size and duration comparisons. The experiments begin at zero-training-loss initializations; the kernel-regime statement is cited prior work.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiments, local-minimum frequency comparisons, or width sweep.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison or test of shortcuts preventing training error degradation.
No initialization comparison or study of initialization-dependent training speed or trainable depth.
No sweep around a stability threshold or test of loss recovery/divergence as a function of learning rate.
No batch-normalization comparison or test of normalization's effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Label-noise SGD initialized from the full-batch global minimizer; randomized label flipping with probability 0.2, cross-entropy, batch size 256, and varied maximum learning rate; no data augmentation or weight decay.

conditions.value: Full Batch Initialization; 100% training accuracy and 76% final test accuracy
maximum learning rate varied; exact values shown in Figure 3

rows.measure: Test accuracy and trace of Hessian over training; text says the run reaches the SGD baseline from this initialization.
rows.baseline: Minibatch SGD baseline with random initialization; exact value not stated.
rows.value: Reaches the SGD baseline from the fullbatch initialization; exact test-accuracy values are not stated in text.
rows.uncertainty: Median over 3 random seeds; shaded error bars denote min/max over the three runs.
rows.note: Outcome concerns test accuracy and Hessian trace after starting at a zero-training-loss initialization; it does not measure whether random initialization training reaches near-zero training error.
rows.check: The outcomes are test accuracy and a curvature proxy, not a claim-version measure. Specify GroupNorm replacing BatchNorm and learning-rate warmup over 300 epochs. The initial 100% training accuracy is a starting condition. Appendix D estimates the regularizer from gradient-noise magnitude rather than directly computing the Hessian trace.
